items.stem: What best distinguishes corporate governance from management?

options.text: Governance directs and oversees the organisation; management runs it day to day
options.rationale: Correct: the board governs and holds management to account.
They are distinct, with different roles and accountabilities.
That is management's role, not governance.

options.text: Management sets strategy and governance executes it

items.explanation: Correct: the board governs and holds management to account.

items.stem: Which features generally strengthen board effectiveness? (Select TWO)

options.text: A sufficient number of independent directors
options.rationale: Correct: independence supports objective oversight of management.

options.text: Specialised committees such as audit and remuneration
options.rationale: Correct: committees allow focused, expert oversight.

options.text: Having the CEO single-handedly control all board decisions

options.rationale: Transparency is a core governance expectation.

items.explanation: Correct: independence supports objective oversight of management.

items.stem: A board reviews risks once at year-end and assumes it is covered. Why is this inadequate?

options.text: Risk oversight must be ongoing, not a one-off annual checklist
options.rationale: Correct: risks evolve continuously and require regular oversight.

options.text: Risk only needs review when something goes wrong
options.rationale: Reactive-only oversight fails to prevent issues.

options.text: Boards have no role in risk
options.rationale: Risk oversight is a core board responsibility.

options.text: Annual review is the maximum ever required
options.rationale: Effective oversight is continuous, not capped at annual.

items.explanation: Correct: risks evolve continuously and require regular oversight.
